Plains/Mountain must add or subtract 1 attack die when the site or anything at the site is targeted, even if attacker rules the site.
Muster at River gives 1 additional warband if you rule it. If you muster there without ruling it, take the ordinary 2 only.
From Provinces to Provinces the base cost is 2; from Charming Valley add 1, so normally 3. If an applicable power says spend no Supply, that final override makes payment 0 despite the increase.
Travel — 1–4 Supply before modifiers|Site powers (Site Reference)

You may use Tribunal’s Action if you rule it or your pawn is there. It enables binding immediate exchanges of favor and secrets and binding future actions with agreed penalties; it does not grant unrestricted immediate relic/banner transfers. If future breach is disputed, settle by coin flip.

Bandit Crown treats bandits as your warbands: they rule empty faceup sites, may pick up the last physical site warband, and can contribute to defense or an attacking force with suitable powers. Bandits cannot be killed, moved, or sacrificed, including by skulls or battle-plan costs.

Facedown sites cannot be ruled and cannot hold cards; a move power cannot place cards there. Both intact and ruined edifices count toward site capacity. A ruin has no suit and cannot be used for Muster or Trade; it does not grant card-power access via a suit.

No. The corrected Draw keyword means take from the top of the prompted source; it does not import Search’s draw-three/stop procedure. Every Vision drawn from world deck advances Visions Drawn, including with Oracle. Search itself still stops at its first world-deck Vision.

During Act you may take any number of major actions, minor actions and Action powers, in any order, repeating or taking none, if you pay costs. Finish an action before starting another. You may end with Supply unspent; Rest refreshes first, then adds leftover Supply, capped at leftmost track space.

A banner seized any way other than Recover loses 2 resources, down to minimum 1; this includes Campaign, Conspiracy, and a transfer that counts as seizure. Conspiracy explicitly applies the seizure penalty. Recover instead requires paying strictly more of the banner’s resource, adds it to banner, and distributes old resources; Recover has no seizure penalty.
Campaign — 2 Supply|Conspiracy|Recover — 1 Supply plus target cost

A plan’s restriction applies to the whole Imperial defending side. The declared defender chooses order, timing and priority when Allies disagree, including which player uses a shared plan and whether a restrictive plan must be declared first. Each shared plan is usable once total per Campaign by one user who pays.

On becoming Citizen, replace all own warbands on board and map with purple; if insufficient purple, the new Citizen chooses which warbands to remove and which to replace. If later exiled by Scepter, replace board purple warbands with own color; existing purple map garrisons stay Imperial.

Normal-side banner at five: the holder must add one if able (the choice is add or return, but its last favor cannot be removed); after that single choice it has six and flips to Mob. No second choice is retroactive. If already Mob at Wake, repeat the same choice twice; the example’s “adds one” alone does not specify the second choice.

completed_events: The single normal-side Wake choice raises the banner from 5 to 6.
result: Flip to Mob at the end of this Wake; do not repeat the choice. If already Mob, make two choices in that Wake.

An unrevealed true Vision cannot win; an Exile must have it revealed and meet its goal at Wake. Revealing it at Wake is a minor action in Act, not Wake, and does not create an immediate victory check. Even with goal complete, no Visionary victory until at least 3 Visions have been drawn from the world deck globally; check at Wake.

No. Oathkeeper title still on its Oathkeeper side at game end is insufficient for Exile Usurper victory. At round 8 priority, Empire wins first if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper; otherwise Usurper wins only if Exile is Usurper; otherwise qualifying revealed Vision wins; otherwise Empire fallback (Citizen Successor may replace Chancellor win).

If the Exile wins through both Usurper and Vision, victory is not by Vision alone, so they may choose any next Oath except the current one. Chronicle Citizenship may be offered by the Exile winner to other Exiles except those just flipped to Exile; not to themself. Each acceptance flips board to Citizen and replaces every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband.

With People’s Favor, discard a card from any site in your region, then play to any site in your region; those sites may differ. The discard must still be from your region, not another region. A locked faceup card cannot be discarded except in Chronicle; respect locks and other discard permissions.

On attacker victory after targeting pawn/favor and a banner, banishment is optional, board-favor burn is independently optional, and taking all targeted banners is mandatory. If choosing favor burn, burn half the defender’s board favor rounded down.

calculation: Optional favor burn is floor(defender board favor ÷ 2).
result: Take the banner; banishment and favor burn are optional. Burn half rounded down only if chosen.

Skulls immediately kill one warband each from the full attacking force, even if you chose fewer attack dice than board warbands; fewer dice do not select a smaller force. Sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 each only if needed, and if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never extra to reduce upkeep.

Exile/Chancellor refresh depends on own warbands remaining in personal bank, not board or map count. Chancellor: 18+ gives 6, 11–17 gives 5, 4–10 gives 4, 0–3 gives 3 Supply. Exile: 9+ gives 6, 4–8 gives 5, 0–3 gives 4. Then add saved unspent Supply by moving marker left one space per unspent point, capped at leftmost/7.

Attacker may use gradient/either and red/attacker-only plans; defender may use gradient/either and blue/defender-only plans. A plan requires ruling its site; rule does not allow using the wrong-color box. Plans are selected by attacker first, then defender.
